guitar.evidence: Extremely well-documented: B.B. King's guitar was named Lucille, primarily a Gibson ES-355 (and later Gibson's own "Lucille" signature model based on the ES-355).
guitar.notes: Original entry is correct and iconic.

tone.target: warm singing blues lead with light vibrato and room reverb
tone.profile: warm singing blues lead with light vibrato and room reverb
tone.summary: A vintage-voiced chain using a low-gain preamp (US Deluxe) paired with an AC30-style amp and room reverb to capture the singing, articulate tone of B.B. King's solo work.
corrections: focus on vocal BB King phrasing

rig.name: B.B. King - Sweet Little Angel (Solo) - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Slightly lift the signal and add warmth without noticeable grit.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used for subtle tone shaping rather than aggressive boost, fitting the 'clean-to-edge' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Provide gentle harmonic saturation and sustain (the 'clean-to-edge' sound) without heavy overdrive.
blocks.gap: Red Haze is chosen for its ability to add grit/sustain gently, mimicking the natural breakup of a vintage tube amp at high volume, rather than aggressive distortion.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the round, articulate tone of a small combo amplifier (like a Fender/Vox style) with plenty of clean headroom.
Provide a bright, articulate, and classic American voicing suitable for blues lead work.
Enhance the round midrange and vocal quality of the tone, focusing on articulation.
Simulate the wide string vibrato characteristic of B.B. King's playing without sounding like a chorus effect.
blocks.gap: While Tremolo is used, its settings are dialed in to act more as a subtle pitch/vibrato enhancer rather than a rhythmic modulation.

blocks.purpose: Add a small, natural room ambiance to give the tone depth and space.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better midrange focus and natural room sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance round, vocal midrange and vintage character.
